title: How to File for Divorce in Georgia (2027): Fees & Steps
rank_math_title: How to File for Divorce in Georgia (2027): 30 Days, $220
rank_math_description: Georgia divorce 2027: 6-month residency, 30 days after service, $220 Fulton County fee, file in your spouse's county, forms, alimony and parenting plans.
focus_keyword: how to file for divorce in georgia
pdf_outline: Checklist: residency 6 mo -> venue (spouse's county) -> settlement agreement / parenting plan / worksheet -> petition + DR case filing info form -> file ($220 Fulton) / indigence affidavit -> acknowledgment of service or sheriff ($50) -> parenting seminar -> 30 days after service -> decree

editor_notes: O.C.G.A. read via FindLaw (justia 403, legis.ga.gov not public). Fulton fee schedule (HB851 citations) shows Divorce $220, Sheriff $50. Venue rule from Ga. Const. art. VI, §2, ¶I; the 'consent to venue' practice varies by county — check local practice. Jury trial on property is permitted in Georgia divorces (not on custody); keep that sentence only if you are comfortable citing O.C.G.A. §19-5-1 / case law.
